extracted.intended_audience: brand owners, marketing managers, and packaging/branding designers in CPG (especially food & beverage)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for planning and evaluating a packaging rebrand for consumer packaged goods (especially juice/food & beverage), focused on avoiding design choices that harm shelf recognition, brand equity, or sales. Covers strategic, visual, and research-related criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Change with a Purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Make sure you have a clear vision of what your goal is before you redesign anything.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define the aesthetic you want, identify your primary and dream buyers, and diagnose why the existing packaging is underperforming. Approach a rebrand with a clear purpose rather than change for change’s sake; purposeful redesigns are more likely to succeed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider Your Audience
rubrics_metrics.description: Every marketing decision needs to center around your target audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Get very clear on who your audience is and what they want. Use surveys, local market research, and focus groups before uprooting an established brand to ensure the redesign resonates with existing buyers and prospective customers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don’t Lose Your Brand / Preserve Recognizable Elements
rubrics_metrics.description: If your brand is known for a specific image, logo, or color, don’t ditch that completely.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep iconic assets (example: Tropicana’s orange-and-white striped straw). Avoid making the brand unrecognizable; tweak existing design elements slowly rather than performing a complete overhaul that severs customer recognition and equity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain Clear Logo Visibility and Legibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure the brand name is bold, visible and easy to find on the front of pack.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid awkward placements or orientations (e.g., flipping words vertically or moving the name to the side) that make the brand hard to find and read quickly on shelf.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visualize Shelf Presence
rubrics_metrics.description: Design must account for how the package will look when displayed on the shelf.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do mockups of front-facing shelf views. Don’t split key images across panels (e.g., splitting a glass or fruit between front and side) because shoppers mostly see the front and need a complete, coherent cue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve Product Cues That Convey Desired Associations
rubrics_metrics.description: Use imagery that communicates the product attributes customers expect (freshness, naturalness, made from real product).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For orange juice, the orange is a go-to image because it evokes freshness and 'made from real oranges.' Replacing such cues (e.g., with a generic glass of yellow liquid) can fail to evoke the intended associations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid Modernizing That Conflicts with Customer Expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not pursue 'modern' or 'edgy' looks if they conflict with what your customers want.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Question whether the target consumers are seeking a modern aesthetic; if not, modernization can alienate buyers. Align stylistic updates with audience preferences rather than designer-driven trends.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don’t Make Customers Work to Find Your Product
rubrics_metrics.description: Packaging should allow shoppers to identify and grab the product quickly without extra effort.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure instant recognition in the aisle — shoppers don’t want to hunt. Losing quick-scan cues (logo, color, iconic imagery) increases friction and reduces purchases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Run Market Research and Test Concepts
rubrics_metrics.description: Pre-launch testing is essential, especially for established brands.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conduct focus groups, surveys, and market-research campaigns to gauge public response and steer design decisions; Tropicana’s failure was linked to a lack of adequate real-world testing before rollout.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retain Brand Personality
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep elements that communicate brand personality and differentiate you from competitors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify which visual or verbal cues carry personality (e.g., Tropicana’s straw) and preserve them or evolve them carefully so the brand retains its distinct identity in the category.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make Incremental Tweaks When Appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: When a brand is established, prefer small, considered changes over radical redesigns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tweak designs slowly and center changes around existing recognizability; incremental evolution reduces the risk of losing loyal buyers and massive sales declines.
